The layer model also puts src/common/filters/** in infrastructure, so this kind of component is expected there. Everything it does is framework or transport work: it catches HttpException, reads the HTTP request and response, works out the language, translates messages with I18nService, and logs failures with winston. The helpers checkIfConstraintAvailable and translateArray only parse and translate class-validator constraint messages. That is technical message formatting, not business rules. The file has no domain invariants, no use-case orchestration and no persistence logic. Formatting HTTP responses could arguably sit in presentation, but the declared layer model explicitly treats filters and pipes as infrastructure.
